sentences.text: February gets an extra day, roughly every four years. Is the calendar broken, or is Earth bad at deadlines?
A normal calendar year has three hundred sixty-five days. But Earth's trip around the Sun takes about three hundred sixty-five and a quarter days.
That leftover quarter is about six hours. After four years, those extra hours add up to roughly one day.
So we add February twenty-ninth. Without this correction, our calendar would slowly drift away from the seasons.
But a quarter day is only approximate. Adding a day every four years would slightly overcorrect.
Century years skip the leap day, unless divisible by four hundred. Two thousand qualified. Twenty-one hundred won't.
So, is February twenty-ninth a bonus day, or Earth's way of asking for an extension?
